cqc_lem.utilities.ai.ai_helper.get_indus.analysis: Six months ago our hospital's discharge process averaged 4.2 hours from physician order to the patient leaving the floor. Everyone blamed transport. When we actually walked the process with a stopwatch, transport was 20 minutes of it. We changed three things. Pharmacy started reconciling likely discharges the evening before. We moved the printer. And the unit clerk now calls the family the moment the physician says 'probably tomorrow', not when the order lands. Average is now 2.1 hours. None of it needed new software. The hardest part was getting people to stop defending the old process long enough to time it. If you run a unit, time one discharge end to end this week.
